nodes.summary: If a trie $t$ is valid, that is, every node has distinct child keys and valid child tries, then for every key $k$ the trie obtained from $t$ by deleting $k$ is valid.
nodes.title: Deletion preserves trie validity

nodes.summary: Deleting a key $k$ (a list of letters) from a trie $t$ works by recursion on $k$. If $k$ is empty, the root of $t$ loses its value and keeps its children. If $k$ consists of a first letter $a$ followed by a key $k'$ and the root of $t$ has no child at $a$, then $t$ is unchanged. Otherwise $k'$ is deleted from the first child at $a$. If the result has neither value nor children, every entry at $a$ is removed from…
nodes.title: Deletion from a trie

nodes.summary: The empty trie is valid.
nodes.title: Validity of the empty trie

nodes.summary: The empty trie is the trie consisting of a single root node that stores no value and has no children, so it contains no key-value entries.
nodes.title: Empty trie

nodes.summary: The entries of a trie are the list of its key-value pairs, where a key is a list of letters. If the root stores a value $v$, the list begins with the pair consisting of the empty key and $v$; it continues, for each child in the stored sibling order, with the entries $(k, w)$ of that child, in order, each rewritten as $(a k, w)$, where $a$ is the letter labelling the child and $a k$ is the key $k$ with $a$ prepended.
nodes.title: Entries of a trie

nodes.summary: If a trie $T$ is valid, then for every key $k$ (a list of letters) and every value $v$, the trie obtained by inserting $v$ at $k$ in $T$ is valid.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves trie validity

nodes.summary: For every trie $T$, all keys $k_1 \ne k_2$ and all values $v_1, v_2$, inserting $v_1$ at $k_1$ and then $v_2$ at $k_2$ gives a trie that is lookup-equivalent to the one obtained by inserting $v_2$ at $k_2$ and then $v_1$ at $k_1$.
nodes.title: Insertions at distinct keys commute in a trie

nodes.summary: Inserting a value $v$ at a key $k$ (a list of letters) in a trie stores $v$ at the node reached by following $k$ from the root, replacing any value stored there. Along the way, a missing child is created as an empty trie and appended after its siblings, an existing child is updated in place, and all other values and children are unchanged.
nodes.title: Trie insertion

nodes.summary: The empty-node test is true on a trie $t$ exactly when $t$ is the node with no value and no children, that is, the empty trie.
nodes.title: Characterization of empty nodes

nodes.summary: The empty-node test is true on a trie node exactly when the node carries no value and has no children; when deletion leaves a child in this state, the child is removed from its parent.
nodes.title: Empty trie nodes

nodes.summary: For every trie $t$ and all keys $k \ne k'$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $t$ by deleting $k'$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $t$.
nodes.title: Deletion does not affect other keys

nodes.summary: For every trie $t$ and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $t$ by deleting $k$ finds no value.
nodes.title: A deleted key is absent

nodes.summary: For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty trie returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty trie

nodes.summary: For every valid trie $T$, every key $k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if $(k, v)$ is one of the entries of $T$.
nodes.title: Trie lookup agrees with the entries

nodes.summary: Two tries $T$ and $T'$ are lookup-equivalent when, for every key $k$, looking up $k$ in $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T'$.
nodes.title: Lookup equivalence of tries

nodes.summary: For every trie $T$, all keys $k \ne k'$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained by inserting $v$ at $k'$ in $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Trie insertion leaves other keys unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality. For every trie $T$ with keys that are lists over $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$, every key $k$ and every value $v \in \beta$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $T$ by inserting $v$ at $k$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup after insertion in a trie

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of letter–trie pairs, $c$ a trie and $a \ne b$ letters, and let $L'$ be obtained from $L$ by setting the child at $b$ to $c$ (removing the entries at $b$ instead when $c$ has neither value nor children). Then looking up $a$ in $L'$ gives the same result as looking up $a$ in $L$.
nodes.title: Setting a child leaves the other children unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of letter–trie pairs, $a$ a letter and $c$ a trie, and let $L'$ be obtained from $L$ by setting the child at $a$ to $c$ (removing the entries at $a$ instead when $c$ has neither value nor children). Looking up $a$ in $L'$ finds nothing when $c$ has neither value nor children, and finds $c$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Looking up a child just set

nodes.summary: The lookup of a key (a list over $\alpha$) in a trie returns an optional value in $\beta$, by recursion on the key. For the empty key it is the optional value stored at the root. For a key with first letter $a$ followed by the key $k$, it fails if no child of the root is labelled $a$, and otherwise it is the lookup of $k$ in the first child labelled $a$.
nodes.title: Trie lookup

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be valid tries with keys that are lists over $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$, and suppose $T$ and $T'$ are lookup-equivalent. Then for every key $k$ and every value $v \in \beta$, the pair $(k, v)$ occurs in the entry list of $T$ if and only if it occurs in the entry list of $T'$.
nodes.title: Lookup-equivalent valid tries have the same entries

nodes.summary: If a trie node with optional value $v$ and child list $c$ is valid, then the letters labelling the children in $c$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Valid trie nodes have distinct child keys

nodes.summary: Every trie is lookup-equivalent to itself.
nodes.title: Reflexivity of trie lookup equivalence

nodes.summary: Let a trie node with value $v$ and child list $L$ be valid, let $c$ be a valid trie and $a$ a letter. Then the node with value $v$ whose child list is obtained from $L$ by setting the child at $a$ to $c$ (removing the entries at $a$ instead when $c$ has neither value nor children) is valid.
nodes.title: Setting a child preserves validity

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of letter–trie pairs whose letters are pairwise distinct and whose tries are all valid, let $c$ be a valid trie and $a$ a letter. Then the list obtained from $L$ by setting the child at $a$ to $c$ (removing the entries at $a$ instead when $c$ has neither value nor children) again has pairwise distinct letters, and every trie in it is valid.
nodes.title: Setting a child preserves the child-list part of validity

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of pairs $(k, c)$ of a key $k$ in $\alpha$ and a trie $c$ (the children of a trie node), let $a$ be a key and $t$ a trie, and call $t$ empty when it carries no value and has no children. Setting the child at $a$ to $t$ in $L$ gives the following list. If no entry of $L$ has key $a$, the result is $L$ itself when $t$ is empty, and $L$ with $(a, t)$ appended at the end otherwise. If some entry of…
nodes.title: Setting a child in a trie's child list

nodes.summary: If a trie $T$ is lookup-equivalent to a trie $T'$, then $T'$ is lookup-equivalent to $T$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of trie lookup equivalence

nodes.summary: If a trie $T_1$ is lookup-equivalent to a trie $T_2$ and $T_2$ is lookup-equivalent to a trie $T_3$, then $T_1$ is lookup-equivalent to $T_3$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of trie lookup equivalence

nodes.summary: A trie with keys that are lists over $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is a node consisting of an optional value in $\beta$ and a finite list of children, each child being a pair of a letter in $\alpha$ and a trie. The letters labelling the children need not be distinct.
nodes.title: Trie

nodes.summary: Validity of tries is defined inductively: a trie node with optional value $v$ and child list $c$ is valid when the letters labelling the children in $c$ are pairwise distinct and every child trie in $c$ is valid.
nodes.title: Valid trie

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
